correctness.rationale: Directly reconstruct the invertible sign transformation to f'=g+f²/2+eta*f, g'=-f with (f,g)(0)=(-2eta,0). The exact identity d(f²+g²)/dX=f²(f+2eta), and Taylor coefficient (4/3)eta³ X³>0, force g>sqrt(4eta²−f²) on the rising negative-f strip, whence f crosses zero in finite time with f'(X0)=g(X0)>2eta>2. For f≥0, f'>2 persists and f''=f(f'−1)+eta f' implies d(f')/df≥eta+f/2. Consequently f'≥f²/4 and the remaining travel time from f=1 is ≤4. Thus f→+∞, original fhat→−∞ in finite forward X. Independent exact Taylor check and representative numerical crossing at eta=1.01,1.5,1.99 corroborate but do not prove the universal theorem.
